_README: Hand-labeled ground truth for codemap's call-graph, per micro-case. Edges are [src, tgt] as suffixes relative to the case package (the harness prepends '<case>.'). 'expected' = call edges a SOUND static analyzer should emit (min_tier: the cheapest tier that can get it — 'fast' or 'deep'); every expected target is a real definition node. 'ceiling' = true call relationships that are statically UNDECIDABLE for any sound tool (higher-order via param, getattr dispatch, registry value-dispatch) — informational, they define the honest recall gap, never penalized. 'limitation' = true relationships codemap does not model by a documented design choice (closure bodies not attributed to a def node; string-registry seams routed through the bridge channel, not as calls edges) — informational, excluded from precision. Targets that are not graph nodes ('phantom') are a soundness signal the harness reports separately; a phantom emitted for a DECIDABLE edge (wrong resolution) counts against precision, a phantom for a limitation edge only raises the soundness flag.

c06_inheritance.note: both tiers resolve self.<inherited>() to the base class that defines it (R1-C13-f1 fixed: _class_members maps each inherited member to its owning-class id, so no phantom same-class target).

c09_registry_dispatch.note: string-keyed dict dispatch — value-flow undecidable as a calls edge; codemap routes such seams through its registry-bridge channel (M7), not as resolved calls.

c10_closure.note: a call inside a closure is attributed to the innermost enclosing definition node (R1-C22 D3, issue #7): outer->helper is emitted on both tiers, carrying extras.via='nested' because the call's *existence* is certain while its source node is an approximation of location. Before R1-C22 the whole closure body was dropped and this edge did not exist — the label recorded that limitation as if it were the right answer, even though this case's own docstring already called outer->helper the resolvable edge. Still not modelled: outer->inner and inner->helper, since `inner` is not a definition node (materializing closure nodes remains future work).

c11_local_import.note: R1-C30: a call through a function-local import. Resolved on both tiers since the fast resolver reads a per-function import map; before it, deep resolved it and fast did not, which read as a deep-only capability and was really a missing map. `elsewhere -> leaf.helper` is deliberately NOT listed anywhere: it is not a true relationship at all (the name is unbound there), so emitting it would count against precision — which is the point of the case, since the cheap way to raise recall here is to merge the local import into the module map and resolve it for every sibling function.

c12_reexport.note: R1-C30-f1 (issue #13): the caller writes `api.helper`, which is not a definition — `api` only re-exports it. Resolved on both tiers now; before it, only deep was, by following the alias, so the fast tier dropped the edge next to sibling calls that resolved. `absent -> api.missing` is deliberately unlisted: the name exists nowhere, so any edge for it counts against precision — the follow may only walk an export edge the structural pass recorded, never guess at a nearby definition.
